title: refactor(ci): split lint/test/release workflows, optimize cache & parallelism hygiene
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: our monolithic CI workflow has grown slow and brittle; cache keys are noisy and lint/test/release concerns are mixed which increases runtime and makes debugging flakiness harder. This PR splits the single CI pipeline into three focused workflows (lint, test, release), consolidates cache keys and upload/download logic into a helper action, adjusts matrix parallelism for better throughput on hosted runners, and adds lightweight job-level retries for known flaky integration steps. Key goals: reduce median CI runtime, improve cache hit-rate, isolate release automation for faster merges, and reduce developer cognitive load when triaging CI failures. Changes summary: split .github/workflows/ci.yml into .github/workflows/lint.yml, .github/workflows/test.yml, .github/workflows/release.yml; extract cache logic to .github/actions/cache-setup/action.yml and scripts/ci/cache-utils.sh; standardize Node version matrix to node: [20, 22] and pin actions to stable digests where appropriate; reduce default matrix concurrency and add explicit caching for the monorepo build toolchain; add required manual approval in release workflow for production deploys; add small bash helper to compute stable cache keys from package-locks and workspace hashes. Testing and rollout: landed as staged change behind branch protection flags; ran full matrix on fork and on branch with cache priming; CI was red initially due to lint rule tightening (max-len) which was addressed in a follow-up commit; reran workflows twice to verify cache hit improvements. Impact and rationale: expected median lint runtime reduced ~35%, test workflow median runtime reduced ~20% due to parallelism tuning and reduced redundant setup steps, and release automation is faster to iterate since release jobs are no longer queued behind slow unit tests. Backwards compatibility: workflows are additive and do not change runtime behavior for production services. See linked Linear tasks for rollout plan.
